status_summary: Since 2025-01-20 the United States has carried out several military operations that began without a prior congressional authorization specific to them, and no enacted authorization for any of them was found: strikes on Houthi-controlled areas of Yemen (reported to Congress in a letter dated 2025-03-28 that cites the President's constitutional authority), strikes on three Iranian nuclear sites (2025-06-21), strikes on suspected drug boats near Venezuela (from 2025-09-02), an operation in Venezuela in which U.S. forces seized its president (2026-01-03), and Operation Epic Fury against Iran (from 2026-02-28, with a ceasefire declared 2026-04-07). The administration has filed War Powers Resolution notifications and has described the boat strikes as part of a non-international armed conflict with designated cartels and the Venezuela seizure as law enforcement. In the Senate, motions to discharge joint resolutions failed on Iran (47-53 on 2025-06-27 and 2026-03-04), on the boat strikes (48-51) and on Venezuela (49-51), while a second Venezuela resolution was discharged 52-47 on 2026-01-08 and then held not privileged on a 50-50 vote with the Vice President voting yea. The House (215-208 on 2026-06-03) and Senate (50-48 on 2026-06-23) agreed to concurrent resolution H.Con.Res. 86 on Iran hostilities, which is not presented to the President and which one report describes as not carrying the force of law under past court precedent, a view some members dispute; a later concurrent resolution passed the House 214-208 and was rejected in the Senate 49-50 on 2026-09-24.

title: Keep war powers divided: Congress decides on war, the executive conducts it
uncertainties: This record describes practice against a principle, not a quantitative target. The diverged label means only that the listed operations began without a prior congressional authorization specific to them and none was enacted afterward; it says nothing about whether the actions were lawful, which is disputed and was not assessed, and Congress also voted down most measures to remove forces. The administration's legal positions are taken from news reports and a presidential letter; the 2026 War Powers reports on Iran were not read. Epic Fury's start date and the ceasefire date come from a Brookings summary. The House vote of 2026-03-05 is from a news report and its resolution number was not checked. The Senate report of the 2026-06-23 vote does not give the resolution number; the vote menu identifies it as H.Con.Res. 86. The vote menu also lists other Iran votes not shown in the timeline: discharge of S.J.Res. 185 agreed 50-47 on 2026-05-19 and a motion to proceed to it rejected 47-50 on 2026-06-24, and motions to discharge S.J.Res. 172 (47-48, 2026-06-16), S.J.Res. 180 (47-49, 2026-07-23) and S.J.Res. 181 (49-50, 2026-07-30) rejected; the menu was read only from mid-May, so earlier 2026 votes may be missing. Other uses of force, such as strikes in Somalia, Syria, Nigeria or Iraq, were not surveyed.
